definition: Consumer relationship systems (CRS) are specialized customer relationship management (CRM) software applications that are used to handle a company's dealings with its customers.
details: Current consumer relationship systems integrate the software with telephone and call recording systems as well as with corporate systems for input and reporting. Customers can provide input from the company's website directly into the CRS. These systems are popular because they can deliver the 'voice of the consumer' that contributes to product quality improvement and that ultimately increases corporate profits. Consumer relationship systems that provide automated support as well as advanced systems may have artificial intelligence (AI) interfaces that can extract and analyse data collected, or handle basic questions and complaints.

explainer.lead: A consumer relationship system gathers a company’s customer interactions in one place, connecting feedback and complaints with its internal systems. It matters because that “voice of the consumer” can guide product improvements and, ultimately, support profits.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a company keeps one big notebook for everything customers tell it by phone or through its website. Staff can read the notes, answer questions, and spot problems that keep coming up. Fixing those problems can make the company’s products better.
tiers.practitioner: A CRS is implemented as specialized CRM software integrated with telephone and call-recording systems, corporate input and reporting systems, and website feedback channels. Optional automated or AI interfaces can answer basic questions and complaints or extract and analyse collected data. The key distinction is that AI is an optional layer, not a requirement of the system.
tiers.paperLevel: A consumer relationship system (CRS) is specialized customer relationship management software for handling a company’s dealings with its customers. Its architecture integrates customer input channels with corporate input and reporting systems; optional automated support and AI interfaces provide data extraction, analysis, or handling of basic questions and complaints. Its stated purpose is to convey the voice of the consumer for product-quality improvement and increased corporate profits.

explainer.example: A customer reports a faulty appliance through the manufacturer’s website, and the complaint enters its CRS directly. An AI interface may handle the basic complaint or analyse the collected report, while the CRS passes the information into corporate systems so the recurring fault can inform product-quality work.

usedIn.name: Corporate reporting
usedIn.detail: Connects customer interactions with corporate systems for input and reporting.

explainer.intuition: Think of a CRS as a company’s shared customer-feedback hub: it collects what customers say, routes that information into business systems, and makes it available for support and analysis.
howItWorks: Customers contact the company by telephone or enter feedback directly through its website.
The CRS gathers these interactions alongside telephone and call-recording information.
It connects the collected information with corporate systems for input and reporting.
Staff, automated support, or optional AI interfaces handle questions and complaints or extract and analyse the data.
The resulting customer feedback contributes to product-quality improvement.
explainer.whyItMatters: A CRS turns customer interactions into information the wider company can use. By bringing the voice of the consumer into product-quality work, it can support improvements that ultimately increase corporate profits.
misconceptions: A CRS is not defined by having AI; automated support and AI interfaces are optional features.
It is not limited to website feedback, because it also integrates telephone and call-recording systems.
It is a specialized form of CRM software, not a completely separate kind of customer-management idea.
